slides.title: Ezra Launches Ezra Loop
slides.highlight: Ezra's launch of a connected human and AI coaching experience aligns with MOSAIC's focus on adaptive AI coaching to improve human proficiency in a coadaptive loop.

slides.title: Counterfactual assessment of social media interventions by separating exposure from engagement
slides.tldr: EXPOSURE VS ENGAGEMENT IN SOCIAL MEDIA INTERVENTIONS
slides.highlight: This work introduces an Exposure--Engagement model to simulate and evaluate social media interventions, distinguishing between recommendation algorithms and user behavior. It is relevant to MIMIC as it provides a framework for analyzing how different intervention strategies impact collective dynamics, such as attention diversity and segregation, in hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Exposure-Engagement model simulates social media interventions, showing algorithmic changes outperform behavioral ones.
card.key_idea: Parametric model separates exposure (recommendation) from engagement (behavior) to simulate counterfactual interventions on collective debate structure.
card.evaluation: Fitted to Italian Twitter data (2018-2022); validated via individual/collective metrics; simulated prebunking, prompts, and chronological feeds.
card.limitation: Model systematically underestimates attention diversity and overestimates segregation; relies on assumptions about effect transfer across platforms.

slides.title: Simulation-Efficient Double-Flow Neural Posterior Estimation for Agent-Based Models
slides.highlight: This work introduces Double-Flow Neural Posterior Estimation (DF-NPE), which reduces the computational cost of Bayesian inference in agent-based models by 90% using synthetic data augmentation. This efficiency is critical for MIMIC's goal of simulating and analyzing large-scale, multi-scale hybrid human-AI societies where likelihoods are often intractable.

card.one_liner: DF-NPE reduces agent-based model simulation costs by 90% using synthetic data augmentation.
card.key_idea: Combines learned time-series summaries with two conditional normalizing flows to generate synthetic training pairs for posterior estimation.
card.evaluation: Tested on Brock-Hommes model; compared to standard NPE using Wasserstein distance and MMD; showed lower discrepancy and runtime.
card.limitation: Performance varies with synthetic-to-direct data allocation and training strategy; relies on accurate learned summary representations.

slides.title: Improving Group Deliberation through AI-Guided Self-Reflection
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that non-directive AI chatbots guiding self-reflection significantly improve group deliberation quality and empathy toward dissenting peers, particularly in disagreements. This aligns with ADAM-CHAT's goal of fostering adaptive, meta-cognitive AI teammates that enhance collective sense-making in human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: AI-guided self-reflection significantly improves subsequent group deliberation quality, especially in disagreeing groups.
card.key_idea: Participants engage in non-directive, Socratic dialogue with an LLM to scaffold self-reflection before joining synchronous, anonymous group policy discussions.
card.evaluation: Randomized trial (N=1,173) measured Discourse Quality Index via LLM-judge; AIR outperformed static/control baselines with moderate effects (d≈0.3).
card.limitation: All group members shared the same condition, ignoring real-world mixed participation; effects rely on specific LLM prompting and automated scoring.

slides.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Co-Adaptive Hip Exoskeleton Control (MARL-Exo) for Metabolic Energy Reduction
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework where a hip exoskeleton co-adapts with a musculoskeletal human model in simulation to reduce metabolic cost, achieving transfer to new users without per-user tuning. This aligns with MOSAIC's goal of closed-loop coadaptation by showing how physics-based human models and AI policies can be jointly optimized for efficient human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: MARL-Exo reduces metabolic cost in new users without per-user tuning via simulation-trained co-adaptive hip exoskeleton control.
card.key_idea: Multi-agent RL co-adapts a full-body musculoskeletal model and hip exoskeleton, optimizing metabolic energy rewards in simulation for sim-to-real transfer.
card.evaluation: Validated in eight adults via indirect calorimetry; showed 18.3% reduction vs passive device and 7.4% vs no-exo, with consistent positive assistance power.
card.limitation: High variance in metabolic reduction (±10.0%) and reliance on simulation fidelity for population-level generalization without individual calibration.

slides.title: Persona AI Brings Calm Experience to Humanoid Startups
slides.highlight: This item highlights Persona AI's focus on calm experiences for humanoid startups, relevant to RwB's work on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: TurnTurk-GPT: Text-Based Turn-Taking Prediction for Turkish
slides.highlight: This work introduces a text-based turn-taking predictor for Turkish that leverages verb-final morphology to detect end-of-turn cues, offering a specialized approach to dialogue segmentation relevant to multimodal social perception systems.

card.one_liner: Fine-tuned Turkish GPT-2 outperforms multilingual detectors for turn-taking, though zero-shot baselines remain competitive.
card.key_idea: Fine-tunes Turkish GPT-2 with TurnGPT objective on synthetic and real dialogues to predict turn-shift probabilities at word boundaries.
card.evaluation: Tested on Real-TurnTurk using AP and cluster bootstrap; outperforms LiveKit detector but matches zero-shot baseline on unseen speakers.
card.limitation: Small dataset (6 speakers) limits generalization; text-only models fail to distinguish pauses from turn-ends, requiring audio cues.

slides.title: Beyond Aggregate WER: In-domain Adaptation, Learner Speech, Code-Switching, and Speaker Attribution in Online Spanish Learning Classrooms
slides.tldr: ASR ADAPTATION FOR LEARNER SPEECH AND DIARIZATION
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that in-domain adaptation of open-weight ASR models significantly improves speaker attribution and transcription accuracy for code-switched learner speech, addressing challenges relevant to HyECHO's goal of robust multimodal social perception in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Condition-aware evaluation reveals ASR struggles with learner speech and code-switching in bilingual classrooms.
card.key_idea: LoRA adaptation on in-domain classroom data improves MOSS significantly, outperforming Whisper and matching commercial Muse.
card.evaluation: Six ASR systems tested on seven held-out Spanish-English sessions using WER, CER, and DER, disaggregated by role and language.
card.limitation: Small sample size (seven sessions) and one institutional context limit generalizability; segmentation differences affect system comparisons.

slides.title: Incongruence-Aware Evaluation of Multimodal Speech Emotion Recognition in Audio Large Language Models
slides.tldr: AUDIO-TEXT INCONGRUENCE DEGRADES LLM EMOTION RECOGNITION
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that incongruence between audio and text channels significantly increases error rates in speech emotion recognition for audio-capable LLMs, a finding critical for HyECHO's goal of robust multimodal social perception in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Audio LLMs suffer higher emotion recognition errors when speech and text signals disagree, unlike supervised classifiers.
card.key_idea: Maps text/audio to shared VAD space; uses GMM to score incongruence, revealing that cross-modal conflict degrades LLM performance.
card.evaluation: Tested three audio LLMs on eNTERFACE, MELD, CMU-MOSEI; validated against human judgment and supervised baselines using logistic regression.
card.limitation: Effect size is modest; results depend on model integration competence, and text-only baselines are confounded by model choice.

slides.title: Confident Fools or Careful Searchers? A Behavioural Study of When LLMs Search Beyond Their Static Internal Memory
slides.highlight: This study audits how commercial LLMs decide between answering from memory and triggering web search, revealing significant variability in search restraint and temporal cue sensitivity. It is relevant to ADAM-CHAT as it highlights the limitations of current models in robustly inferring when external information is needed, a key challenge for adaptive agents requiring reliable self-monitoring and tool-use calibration.

card.one_liner: A benchmark auditing when commercial LLMs correctly trigger web search versus answering from internal memory.
card.key_idea: Evaluates search decisions on 400 questions using Net Awareness and Knowledge Integrity scores to measure selective tool usage.
card.evaluation: Tested five commercial LLMs on news-based questions; results show high selectivity for GPT-5 mini and Grok 4 Fast.
card.limitation: Search triggering is partly driven by temporal cues rather than true metacognition, and vendor-specific search stacks confound comparisons.

slides.title: When Does GenAI Use Support Critical Thinking? A Cross-Cultural Structural Account of Transactive Memory with GenAI
slides.tldr: TMS FRAMEWORK FOR HUMAN-AI CRITICAL THINKING
slides.highlight: This paper extends Transactive Memory Systems theory to human-AI partnerships, identifying how dividing and coordinating cognitive labor with GenAI supports critical thinking, which informs HyECHO's modeling of hybrid team dynamics.

card.one_liner: GenAI supports critical thinking through active output reworking and coordinated labor division, not mere tool exposure.
card.key_idea: Extends Transactive Memory Systems to human-AI partnerships, modeling how familiarity drives specialization and reflective transformation.
card.evaluation: Surveyed 891 US and Turkish students using structural equation modeling; found largely invariant results across cultures.
card.limitation: Cross-sectional design limits causal inference; relies on self-reported data from college students in two specific countries.

slides.title: When Architectural Spaces Start to Act
slides.highlight: This paper explores how architectural robots reshape spatial conditions, extending human-robot interaction beyond momentary actions to long-term inhabitation and control, which informs the design of embodied social robots in dynamic environments.

card.one_liner: Architectural robots shape spaces through persistent spatial consequences, requiring new interaction models beyond motion.
card.key_idea: Interaction extends beyond robotic motion to the spatial configurations that persist, affecting inhabitability, control, and shared occupancy.
card.evaluation: Reflective analysis drawing on prior co-design and in-the-wild studies of robotic partitions and benches; no new quantitative results.
card.limitation: Lacks empirical data on long-term inhabitation of multi-robot environments and specific negotiation mechanisms for conflicting needs.

slides.title: Beyond Utterance-Level Speaker Similarity: Perception-Aligned Segmental Evaluation of Accent in Speech Generation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a segmental evaluation protocol that localizes perceived accent differences in generated speech, offering finer-grained perceptual insights than utterance-level similarity ratings. Such detailed analysis of speech generation artifacts is relevant to HyECHO's goal of understanding hybrid human-AI team dynamics through precise social perception.

card.one_liner: Introduces segmental accent evaluation via subword annotations, revealing weak correlation with existing objective metrics.
card.key_idea: Combines utterance-level SMOS with subword annotations of perceived accent differences from target-region listeners to locate specific pronunciation errors.
card.evaluation: 47 listeners rated 200 pairs from Scottish/Australian voices and TTS systems; compared against seven objective distances using Spearman correlation.
card.limitation: Modest inter-annotator agreement and limited speaker/sample size; objective metrics show weak correspondence with segmental annotations.

slides.title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
slides.highlight: This work introduces a metacognitive controller for diffusion language agents that optimizes inference efficiency by adapting token generation based on environmental interaction needs, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's goal of self-monitoring and efficient adaptive agents.

card.one_liner: A metacognitive controller reduces diffusion agent inference FLOPs by 20.6% while maintaining accuracy.
card.key_idea: Lightweight controller guides decoding via confidence alignment for structural tokens and flux policy to shrink active computation ranges.
card.evaluation: Tested on BFCL and multi-hop QA; outperforms baselines in FLOPs reduction with competitive accuracy across five benchmarks.
card.limitation: Controller adaptation to evolving diffusion models remains an open challenge; relies on specific agent trajectory patterns.

slides.title: Scaling Smart: How LLM Developers Are Solving Multi-Agent Orchestration Bottlenecks
slides.highlight: This article addresses bottlenecks in coordinating multiple LLM agents, a key challenge for MIMIC's goal of simulating harmonious hybrid human-AI societies.

slides.title: Tairex Launches Multi-Agent AI System to Transform Clinical Collaboration and Decision Support
slides.tldr: MULTI-AGENT AI FOR CLINICAL DECISION SUPPORT
slides.highlight: Tairex has launched a multi-agent AI system designed to enhance clinical collaboration and decision support, offering insights into how coordinated agent architectures can improve complex decision-making processes.

slides.title: FOCUS: First-Order Control Using Optimal Transport Supervision for Imitation from Observations
slides.highlight: FOCUS demonstrates how local optimal-transport alignment can stabilize imitation learning from state-only observations in contact-rich tasks, offering a potential mechanism for aligning human-AI intent in MOSAIC's coadaptive loop without requiring temporally aligned trajectories.

card.one_liner: FOCUS enables stable imitation from unaligned state-only observations via optimal transport and differentiable simulators.
card.key_idea: Combines local optimal-transport alignment with soft best-of-K expert segment selection and short-horizon actor-critic learning to derive differentiable imitation rewards.
card.evaluation: Tested on DFlex locomotion tasks (including SNU Humanoid) against adversarial and differentiable baselines, showing improved sample efficiency and stability.
card.limitation: Requires a known differentiable simulator; validated only on periodic locomotion, leaving manipulation and real-world transfer unaddressed.

slides.authors: João A. Cândido Ramos et al.

slides.title: Assuring Learning-Enabled Cyber-Physical Systems with Foundation Models: A Neuro-Symbolic Agenda for Testing, Verification, and Runtime Assurance
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a neuro-symbolic assurance stack for learning-enabled cyber-physical systems, aligning with MIMIC's focus on integrating symbolic reasoning with neural models for trustworthy agent behavior.

card.one_liner: Proposes a neuro-symbolic assurance stack for foundation-model-enabled cyber-physical systems.
card.key_idea: Shifts to system-level assurance via symbolic world models, conformance testing, and compositional verification with runtime monitoring.
card.evaluation: Conceptual agenda based on Shonan Seminar discussions; no empirical experiments or quantitative results reported.
card.limitation: High complexity in maintaining abstraction fidelity and composing evidence across stochastic and formal boundaries.

slides.title: Making Sense of Audience Change: Causal Attribution and Boundary Management on Xiaohongshu
slides.tldr: CAUSAL ATTRIBUTION AND BOUNDARY MANAGEMENT IN SOCIAL PLATFORMS
slides.highlight: This study examines how users attribute community changes and manage boundaries on recommendation-driven platforms, offering insights into the social dynamics and governance consequences of audience restructuring that are relevant to understanding hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Users attribute audience shifts to algorithms or social actors, aligning strategies with perceived problem sources.
card.key_idea: Thematic and quantitative analysis of Xiaohongshu comments links causal attributions to boundary management strategies via permutation tests.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 262 comments from eight threads; strong association (Cramér’s V=.583) between algorithmic attributions and technical strategies.
card.limitation: Small, purposive sample from specific threads limits generalizability; association does not establish causal relationships.

slides.title: From Leniency to Suspicion: How an Open Post-Training Recipe Changes Whom LLM Fact-Checkers Believe
slides.tldr: Post-training induces job-based bias in LLM fact-checkers
slides.highlight: This study reveals that specific open post-training recipes can induce subtle but reliable job-based bias in LLM fact-checking, altering how models interpret poster identity. This is relevant to HyECHO as it highlights the need to monitor how training procedures affect social perception and addressee modeling in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: The open Tülu-3 post-training recipe uniquely induces LLMs to doubt claims from lower-status job posters.
card.key_idea: Tülu-3 SFT rewires the model's interpretation of occupational status, flipping base leniency toward lower-status posters into suspicion via a single residual-stream direction.
card.evaluation: Tested on PolitiFact claims across six model families and seven commercial APIs; effect is <1% but statistically reliable, replicated, and confirmed via activation steering.
card.limitation: Effect is recipe-specific and tiny; mechanism shown only in one model; commercial models show no such bias, limiting generalizability to deployed systems.

slides.title: BioAgent: Self-Directed Skill Acquisition and Capability Growth for Long-Horizon Laboratory Protocols
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates an embodied agent for laboratory protocols that aligns with MOSAIC's focus on incremental skill acquisition and human-AI coadaptation by integrating human teaching requests with validated skill packages and autonomous recovery mechanisms.

card.one_liner: BioAgent autonomously acquires missing skills and validates experimental validity for long-horizon laboratory protocols.
card.key_idea: Matches protocol requirements to validated skills, targets capability gaps via tool-based learning, and enforces validity-aware recovery.
card.evaluation: Tested on two dual-arm tasks (20/31 steps); 66%/58% success with recovery, outperforming baselines in atomic skill reliability.
card.limitation: Complete-task success remains moderate (58-66%), with failures concentrated in precise alignment and liquid-state handling.

slides.title: REA: A Routed Embodied Agent Runtime for Asynchronous Brain-Cerebellum Control
slides.highlight: This paper introduces REA, a runtime that decouples slow deliberative reasoning from fast reactive control to prevent stalling, a coordination challenge relevant to the asynchronous human-robot interaction goals of RwB.

card.one_liner: REA unifies slow reasoning agents and fast policies via a non-blocking router, achieving 95.9% success on LIBERO-Pro.
card.key_idea: A three-level runtime where a router selects policies from memory and consults an agent only at boundaries, ensuring no policy waits on the brain.
card.evaluation: Tested on LIBERO-Pro, RoboTwin 2.0, BEHAVIOR-1K, and real robots; outperforms baselines in success rate and control time with statistical significance.
card.limitation: Relies on pre-computed route memory from development episodes and incurs extra wall-clock time when the visual judge gate is triggered.
